answer: We model an anti-Sybil mechanism where staking nodes must commit capital to a multi-asset pool containing copper and security-token collateral, governed by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. To exploit this relic of early design, an adversary faces quadratic slashing penalties that scale super-linearly with cluster size, rendering attack utility negative. By forcing a falcon signature threshold where marginal attack costs far exceed extractable value, the protocol sustains a robust Nash equilibrium.
